LEARNING PATH · CLASS 42 · MEASURING & MONEY · AGES 4–5

Measuring & Money — twenty-eight printable math cards to download and print.

Twenty-eight printable math flashcards for ages four to five, all on this one page, in five shelves: counting and adding, measuring and comparing, position words, sorting and matching, and the shapes-fractions-money finish. Every card carries its rule in words YOU can say back — count each thing one time; parts make the whole; the side that goes down is heavier — with Download and Print buttons right under the picture. Pick a card, print it, and the math walks off the page: a ruler at breakfast, coins at the store, pairs of socks on the bed.

Back to the Learning Path ↗
HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

One math idea. The child says it. Then the day does the teaching.

Every card prints one early-math idea the way a four-year-old meets it: how many things there are, how long the table is, which backpack is heavier, how many coins make a treat. The small words under each picture are the rule itself, said kid-first — count each thing one time, take away to find what is left, make pairs to check. The Download button saves the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer. Math words grow the same way the cards run — small, happy and repeated.

The shelves follow a math day. The count-and-add shelf counts to 10 and to 20, splits numbers into bonds and bundles, sorts odd from even, and puts groups together and takes them away. The measure-and-compare shelf weighs, measures and sizes up the whole house. The position-words shelf is the treasure map — left, right, inside, outside, in front, behind, top, bottom. The sort-and-match shelf compares groups and finds what belongs together. And the last shelf is the big finish: shapes, fair-share fractions, money math and the day-and-night clock.

THE COUNT & ADD SHELF · 7 CARDS

Count it, add it, take it away.

The number cards families print first: counting to 10 and to 20, number bonds, tens and ones, odd and even, and the plus-and-minus pair. Counting flashcards for preschool math that start at one apple. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer. Every pill answers one question: the age, the subject, the grade level, the skill it builds.

THE MEASURE & COMPARE SHELF · 9 CARDS

How long, how heavy, how much fits.

Measurement for beginners: long and short, the ruler, height, heavy and light, the balance scale, thick and thin, wide and narrow, full and empty, near and far — measuring activities for kids that use the whole house. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer. Every pill answers one question: the age, the subject, the grade level, the skill it builds.

THE POSITION WORDS SHELF · 4 CARDS

Where is it? Say it like a treasure map.

Position words for kindergarten: left and right, inside and outside, in front and behind, top and bottom — the words that turn "over there!" into a map you can follow. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer. Every pill answers one question: the age, the subject, the grade level, the skill it builds.

THE SORT & MATCH SHELF · 4 CARDS

Same or different? More or less?

Comparing and classifying: same and different, sorting and grouping, more and less, and equal — the matching games that quietly build logic. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer. Every pill answers one question: the age, the subject, the grade level, the skill it builds.

THE SHAPES, FRACTIONS & MONEY SHELF · 4 CARDS

Shapes, fair shares and the piggy bank.

The big-kid finish: circle, square, triangle and rectangle, simple fractions with pizza and chocolate, money math with coins, price and change — and the day-and-night clock that times it all. Download takes the full-size card; Print runs just that one card through the printer. Every pill answers one question: the age, the subject, the grade level, the skill it builds.

AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where the math learning grows.

Counting lessons in Class 35 · Ages 4–5 ↗Comparing words in Class 19 · Ages 3–5 ↗Measuring like a scientist in Class 31 · Ages 4–5 ↗Time & Daily Routine in Class 41 · Ages 4–5 ↗The Learning Path ↗

Class 35 counts one apple to twenty figs, Class 19 races the opposites — big and small, full and empty — and Class 31 measures like a scientist with balances and rulers in the Science, Nature & Discovery class. This class adds the measuring tools, the money and the position words to the same skills. And when the day needs a schedule, Class 41 · Time & Daily Routine prints the clock and the routine cards beside these.

Math is not a worksheet — it is a measuring cup. Every card here hands the math words to you — the counting, the comparing, the coins — and your grown-up’s whole job is to hand you the ruler.
